detail.data_required: EODHD /div with declarationDate, across a survivorship-free US universe including delisted tickers; daily bars already held
detail.rationale: Two mechanisms, both about who is forced to act. (1) Management avoids cutting a dividend almost to the point of irrationality, so a cut is a costly signal of private information about deterioration -- it is believed precisely because it hurts to send. (2) Dividend-mandated holders (income funds with a yield requirement, retirees drawing an income) must sell regardless of price, and they cannot wait for a better one. Forced sellers who cannot wait are the only reliable source of an edge at retail size. Not arbitraged away because the capacity is small and the trade is short-side, which most retail capital cannot take.

author: claude-opus-5

detail.rationale: Not novel and not claimed to be -- the point is the COST argument. Every other candidate in the register dies on transaction cost at EUR 10k. A rule trading one ETF two to four times a year pays ~10 bps/yr in total, against the 45 bps PER TRADE that kills stock-level strategies. An edge can be largely decayed and still clear that bar, so a documented, crowded effect is worth measuring here where it would not be elsewhere. Mechanism claimed in the literature: slow diffusion of macro information plus institutional risk limits that force de-risking after drawdowns.

summary: Lookback grid 50-300 days x 2 ETFs x 3 sample windows (full, first half, second half). Signal acted on the next session's close; 10 bps per switch

author: claude-opus-5

detail.reason: Fails the stated bar at every single parameter. Beats buy-and-hold on return at 0 of 6 lookbacks on SPY and 0 of 6 on QQQ, in the full sample AND in both halves separately; median shortfall -3.80%/yr on SPY and -5.00%/yr on QQQ. The risk-adjusted claim does hold -- Sharpe 0.59 -> 0.72 and max drawdown -55% -> -20% on SPY -- so the literature is not wrong, it is answering a different question. Converting that Sharpe into a return advantage needs leverage: levered to the index's own volatility it gives +1.27%/yr on SPY and +0.36%/yr on QQQ, which is a coin-flip before any borrowing cost, and leverage is forbidden by the mandate. Cost was never the binding constraint here, which is the useful part: this rejection is about the signal, not about account size, so it would not be rescued by more capital.

author: claude-opus-5
summary: Round 1, full survivorship-free universe: 3,580 declared cuts, 1,678 inferred omissions, horizons 5-252d. INVALID -- the placebo of random dates drifted -3.11% at 126d (clustered t -3.33), so the measurement had a contaminated baseline

author: claude-opus-5
summary: Round 2, liquid names only ($2M/day). Placebo improved but still carried a +562% mean at 21d against a -0.67% median -- one broken price series

author: claude-opus-5
summary: Round 3, liquid AND price-screened. 1,710 declared cuts across 1,094 tradable symbols, measured as median abnormal return against a placebo baseline

author: claude-opus-5

detail.reason:
No effect once measured against the right baseline, and two pre-registered kill criteria fired.
(1) EXCESS OVER PLACEBO IS ZERO. Declared cuts show -1.12% median abnormal return at 63 days with a clustered t of -2.31, which looks significant -- but a placebo of random dates in the same universe shows -1.03%. The excess is -0.09%. At 126 and 252 days cutters do BETTER than the placebo (+0.60%, +3.07%). The apparent significance was measuring the universe's drift against SPY, not the event. Without the placebo this would have been reported as a real 1.1% effect.
(2) SPLIT-HALF SIGN FLIP at 2 of 5 horizons (21d: +0.75% early, -1.01% late; 126d: +2.15% early, -2.82% late). Pre-registered kill criterion.
(3) CUT-SIZE GRADIENT RUNS BACKWARDS, monotonically: 25-40% cuts -3.24%, 40-60% -0.90%, 60-80% +0.15%, 80-100% +0.88%. The most severe cuts perform BEST. A real mechanism scales with severity; this is the mechanism's own prediction inverted, which is stronger evidence against than a null result would be.
Inferred omissions look more negative (-2.06% median at 63d) but their event date is an inference, not an observation, and their excess over the same placebo is only -1.03%. Not enough to rescue anything.

author: claude-opus-5

detail.data_required: EODHD /div with declarationDate; first-bar dates to exclude prior payers
detail.rationale: The forced-BUYER mirror of N2, and the better fit for a long-only mandate. Funds with an income mandate may hold only dividend payers, so a company becoming one is mechanically bought by a class of investor previously barred from owning it -- and they buy on the calendar, not on the price. It is also a costly signal in the same sense a cut is: management binds itself to a recurring payment it will be punished for withdrawing, which is not something a board does about earnings it does not expect to persist.

summary: Stocks outperform the index in the weeks after initiating their first dividend, measured from the declaration date

author: claude-opus-5
summary: 276 genuine initiations across 1,963 tradable symbols, horizons 5-252d, measured as median abnormal return against a placebo baseline. 2,056 of 2,332 first-observed dividends discarded because the company may have been paying before its data begins

author: claude-opus-5

detail.reason:
THE SIGN IS BACKWARDS. Predicted positive; observed -1.33% excess at 63 days (clustered t -2.49) and -4.19% at 252 days (clustered t -2.99). Initiators UNDERPERFORM, and they do so consistently in both sample halves at 63, 126 and 252 days.
There is a plausible story for the inverted result -- a company initiating a dividend is signalling it has run out of things to invest in, which is a life-cycle maturity signal rather than a confidence signal. IT IS NOT CLAIMED AS AN EDGE AND MUST NOT BE. Flipping a hypothesis's sign after seeing the data, in a 276-event sample, is precisely the data mining this protocol exists to prevent. If it is worth anything it is worth pre-registering as its own hypothesis and testing on data this one did not touch.
It is also a short signal, which a long-only cash-equity mandate cannot act on except by declining to buy -- the same dead end as N2.

author: claude-opus-5
summary: Cost-mitigation grid: 4 hold sizes x 4 buy/hold bands, Novy-Marx and Velikov's spread. Best cell (hold 50, band 10) returns +1.10%/yr over SPY overall -- and loses 2.84%/yr in the first half

author: claude-opus-5

detail.reason:
Fails the decision rule fixed before the grid was run: accept only if the SAME configuration beats SPY in BOTH sample halves. ZERO of 16 cells do. Every single one loses in the first half, by 2.84 to 17.0 points.
The best cell shows +1.10%/yr over SPY and is exactly what the rule exists to catch: best-of-16 selection on a result that is -2.84% in the first half and +5.15% in the second. That is a regime bet wearing a backtest.
Cost mitigation worked as documented -- the buy/hold spread cut turnover from 51% to 37% and cost drag from 2.99% to 2.12%/yr -- it just was not the problem.
Risk makes it worse than the return gap suggests: 42.1% volatility against SPY's 18.6%, and a -52.0% drawdown against -35.2%. On EUR 10,000 that is EUR 5,200 gone at the trough versus EUR 3,520 for holding the index. Even if the return gap closed exactly, the trade would be 2.3x the volatility and 20 names instead of 500 in exchange for matching the index.
